title: Evaluating Depth Sectioning and its Systematic Errors in Multislice Ptychography
content: Achieving robust three-dimensional imaging has been a long-standing challenge in electron microscopy. The development of aberration correctors allowed the use of large numerical apertures that scaled down the depth-of-focus to a few nm, enabling the acquisition of a through-focal series for 3D imaging. However, the through-focal strategy has severe limitations in imaging crystalline samples due to the channeling effect of the electron beam, resulting in depth-dependent contrast and systematic errors in atomic positions (for example, the location of a dopant atom embedded in a matrix) [1, 2]. Both these limitations have been addressed by solving the inverse problem of electron scattering, including multiple-scattering and channeling effects, in multislice electron ptychography (MEP) [3], providing robust 3D structural information [4-6].
